title: Hail, Full of Grace, Virgin Theotokos
description: Hail, Full of Grace, Virgin Theotokos in Tonic Solfa to PENITENTIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904), headed “Theotokion”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Tens (10.10.10.10), and this page sets them to PENITENTIA; any other Tens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hail, full of grace, Vir-gin The-o-to-kos, Har-bour of all who on the bil-lows toss; Re-fuge of those who help-less seek Thy grace, Hope-less and sin stained of our fall-en race.

lines: Hail, full of grace, Virgin Theotokos,
Harbour of all who on the billows toss;
Refuge of those who helpless seek Thy grace,
Hopeless and sin-stained of our fallen race.
From thee the Lord Incarnate came to free
Those who are held in bands of misery.
Hail! Virgin Mother, for alone thou art
Blessèd for ever, by each human heart.
Say to the Christ that strife of sin should cease,
That to this world should come the bliss of peace.
Hail! full of grace, Virgin to thee be praise,
Now and for ever through the endless days.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to PENITENTIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
